title: Capture golden state
summary: Capture a new golden through the governed operation to seal current cause-bearing probes. On macOS it first closes every running identity browser through its DevTools port, never force-quitting, so its cookie store is on disk; Linux and WSL capture asks every Chromium to quit. Either refuses test_machine_sign_in_app_quit_not_proved when a browser stays open. Harness logins and the identity store (~/.yoke-browser-identities) stay outside every golden, so an older golden never restores a stale sign-in. Safari's cookie store and the snap Chromium store are no longer kept; a sealed macOS golden that still declares the Safari entry stays resettable through RETIRED_PRESERVED_HOME_ENTRIES. macOS capture also prunes Library/Caches because the OS changes cache files during copying; this capture-only exclusion never enters the preserved manifest, so reset clears caches instead of keeping them live. Tar stderr still fails capture. Saving a completed harness sign-in is this same capture. This is source behavior; live capture and reset proof on real hosts remains pending. Capture refuses golden_capture_insufficient_space before writing when the destination filesystem cannot hold the home, and after the new golden is registered it deletes every retired snapshot except that golden, every golden any project registered for the same host and user (named by the server as kept_golden_paths), anything newer than that golden, and their probes, probe digests (GOLDEN.probes.sha256), manifests and harness CLI version records (GOLDEN.harness-clis), first clearing each sealed snapshot's macOS deny-delete ACLs and making its directories owner-writable; when the server cannot name those goldens, or another registered name for the same host and user is leased, it deletes nothing and refuses golden_snapshot_retention_failed. Verify first checks that every golden registered for its host and user exists and refuses registered_golden_missing, naming each project and path and teaching a new capture for that project; never delete or move a registered golden by hand. Capture writes the version record from each harness CLI's --version as the test user and repeats it on the receipt as harness_cli_versions; an unreadable version refuses golden_harness_cli_version_unreadable. An undeclared nonzero probe exit retries once with both attempts retained; a declared failure stops immediately. macOS copy tools use en_US.UTF-8 independently of the SSH caller locale. Copy failure recovery quotes a short diagnostic excerpt, points to the full copy_stderr receipt field and asks for repair of its actual cause before a new destination capture. A remaining locale warning means the host lacks the locale the copy tools already set; check locale -a on the host and repair its locale installation. Every test-machine status:error receipt exits nonzero. Linux and WSL capture read GOLDEN.probes back over the same transport and refuse golden_probes_write_unverified, before the golden is registered, unless its byte count and sha256 match what was sent; the upload itself decodes strictly and refuses a short write with golden_probes_write_failed. Reset names why sealed probes are unusable: baseline_probes_unavailable with the path when the file is missing, empty or unreadable, or baseline_probes_invalid with the parse exception, byte count, sha256 and the sealed expected_sha256.
